title: SSE scan_from overlap comment explains bytes not chars
description:
client.rs subscribe_events: comment says 'scan_from is set to old_len.saturating_sub(3)... 3 bytes back covers the longest incomplete delimiter prefix that can straddle a chunk boundary: 
 (prefix of 

)'. But scan_from is an index into a String (char boundary in UTF-8), not a raw byte count, and old_len is buf.len() (bytes). The scan_from walk-back loop then adjusts to a char boundary. The comment is accurate about the 3-byte overlap but a contributor might confuse why we walk back to a char boundary if we're counting bytes. The comment should note that the 3-byte overlap is in bytes, which is safe because  and 
 are single-byte codepoints — no char boundary adjustment is ever needed for these specific delimiters.
